expectation.note: Seven months a year, not twelve. Contrast Stripe's billing anchor, which bills the last day of the month instead, and relativedelta/Temporal 'constrain', which clamp to the 28th/30th.

normative_evidence.quote: Recurrence instances falling on invalid dates and times are ignored and not counted as part of the recurrence set.

normative_evidence.note: splits that sentence: invalid *dates* keep the MUST-ignore treatment; nonexistent *local times* are routed to §3.3.5 instead

rationale: The single most consequential month-end divergence in the corpus, because three defensible semantics exist — omit (RFC), clamp (Temporal constrain, relativedelta, Stripe), drift (naive iterated addition) — and only the first is RFC-conformant.
title: BYMONTHDAY=31: months without a 31st are omitted
